side_a: CC 3.2: "A portable root minted by any trio enters via delegation. The shipped default enters via ceremony."
side_b: CC 4.4.3.8: "It is minted by the [CC 4.2.1](#4.2.1) conferral ceremony and owes nothing to any prior root."
note: Who mints a portable root and on which plane: CC 3.2 T2 says any trio, entering by delegation; CC 4.4.3.8 and CC 4.2.1 say the conferral ceremony, a co-scrub by a strict majority of the standing accord roster. CC 3.2 T2 itself says root identity is conferred by ceremony, so the rest of the text supports side B.

side_a: CC 3.2: "Consumers pin `community_key_id: ciris-canonical` and resolve the live member set via `resolve_community`"
side_b: CC 4.4.3.8: "That names the founders of `ciris-canonical`, who are the three accord holders `A1`, `B1`, `C1`"
note: Whose signatures the shipped default pin trusts: CC 3.2 (and CC 5.3.4) resolve the live member set, which by CC 3.2 includes serve nodes seated as role member; CC 4.4.3.8 says the pin names the founders and never a serving install's key. The same paragraph also writes the pin as a policy value where CC 4.4.3.8 says the set is the reader's own acceptance edges and nothing else. CC 3.2 "Infrastructure does not vote" supports the founders reading.

side_a: CC 4.4.1: "the consumer MUST also weight `witness_relation: self` claims against the attester's other-emission track record"
side_b: CC 2.1: "Consumers weight by relation, so that self-attestation cannot game a verdict."
note: CC 4.4.1 states a MUST and gives CC 3.4.7 as its home; the member's own entry in CC 2.1 is descriptive and names no track-record test, and I did not find the MUST in the opening of CC 3.4.7. The duty has no home statement.

side_a: CC 4.1.1: "Consumer policy SHOULD cap the trust weight any single terminal delegate can accumulate from a given root attester at **0.5 × root_trust** by default"
side_b: CC 6.1.8: "the CC 4.1.1 **aggregate-weight cap** (default 0.5 × root_trust) MUST bound the standing one root confers transitively"
note: SHOULD at the home, MUST in the restatement that cites it. C135 reads them as two cases (general policy, and the one bootstrap mechanism); the restatement still names the home's cap as its own.

side_a: CC 6.1.8: "trust-graph **cycles MUST be rejected** (CC 4.1.1)"
side_b: CC 4.4.3.8: "Cycles are visited once, and the cap holds whatever a licensor carries."
note: Reject against visit once. C246 reads them as two graphs (capability delegations, acceptance edges); CC 6.1.8 says "trust-graph", the word CC 4.4.3.8 uses for the acceptance graph.

side_a: CC 4.4.3.12: "Consumer trusts an attestation if `attesting_key_id` has been vouched for by the pinned trust set."
side_b: CC 4.4.3.8: "At each hop the remaining depth is the lesser of what is left and the edge's own."
note: Policy B "adds one hop" over Policy A, yet Policy A already walks to the depth each entry carries (0 to 5). How B's one hop relates to an entry's depth is unstated.

side_a: CC 4.4.3.8: "who are the three accord holders `A1`, `B1`, `C1`"
side_b: CC 4.2.3: "The slot stays as specified; the count is an instance parameter."
note: CC 4.4.3.8 writes the count and the seat names into the recommended default; CC 4.2.3 and constants.tsv (accord_holder_count: N, 3 at the seed) make it a parameter. Near C040, which covers CC 4.2.3 and CC 5.3.4 only.

side_a: CC 6.1.5.3: "Every CIRIS node is **claimed** before it operates on the mesh in normal operation"
side_b: CC 3.2: "With no owner, a key MAY trust and serve `infrastructure` communities and does nothing more."
note: One says every node is claimed before it operates; the other gives an unowned key a floor of operation. C217 reads CC 6.1.5.3 as setting a cohort's audience only; "in normal operation" is the hedge that carries it.

side_a: CC 3.4.7.3: "the granter of the one live owner-binding `delegates_to`, and nothing else"
side_b: CC 3.4.7.3: "The `identity_occurrence` half yields **at most one** anchor, and the custody half yields **at most one**"
note: Whether an identity_occurrence makes its identity a steward for Clause D. The definition and CC 3.2 (the folds never read occurrences) say no; the Cardinality paragraph counts an occurrence anchor. An agent would be admitted to act through a node on one reading and refused on the other.

side_a: CC 2.4.1.2: "A `delegates_to(user → node/agent)` carrying `delegation_purpose: owner_binding` is the owner-binding"
side_b: CC 3.4.13: "Guardianship of a minor and stewardship of an agent share one wire predicate and nothing else: the owner-binding `delegates_to` that `is_steward_bound` folds"
note: CC 2.4.1.2 gives the owner-binding a node or agent target only; CC 3.4.13 and CC 3.4.12 put the same row on a user target (a minor, an adult under an order). A write gate built from CC 2.4.1.2 alone refuses the guardianship row. CC 3.2 supports the wider target.

side_a: CC 2.4.1.1: "A node MUST admit a `withdraws` against a target row `T` when one line of this table holds"
side_b: CC 3.2: "A node MUST reject a rule-2 or rule-4 `withdraws` against a live owner-binding unless it carries a `wa_adjudication_ref`."
note: The home table gives rule 2 one condition (the kept list) and says a node MUST admit when a line holds. CC 3.2 adds a second condition for one family. Built from CC 2.4.1.1 alone, a node admits a compromised node key's withdrawal of its own owner. CC 3.2 is the specific rule; the home neither states nor cites the gate.

side_a: CC 2.4.1.1: "a retroactive identity claim that promotes a canonical hash to a real `key_id`, which opens rule 2"
side_b: CC 3.3.14: "it does not admit a `withdraws` from `K` against a target naming `H`"
note: Whether a key that has bound itself to a canonical hash may withdraw rows naming that hash. CC 2.4.1.1 says the binding opens rule 2; CC 3.3.14 says the binding admits nothing and the route is the rule-3 proxy.

side_a: CC 2.4.1.1: "Its later `withdraws` against any row carrying that hash in `subject_key_ids` is admitted under rule 3."
side_b: CC 3.3.14: "The proxy attaches only after that out-of-band establishment, reaches no row on the kept list of CC 2.4.1.1, and is suspended while two bindings for the same person compete."
note: CC 2.4.1.1 lets the data-holding agent set the proxy up by its own delegates_to and admits its later withdrawal with no further test. CC 3.3.14 adds two conditions: identity established out of band first, and suspension while bindings compete. A withdrawal is admitted on one reading and refused on the other. Beside C276, which covers the binding and not the proxy's conditions.

side_a: CC 3.4.1: "Revocation rides the tombstone, `withdraws`/`recants`, supersession, or the halt latch, and nothing else."
side_b: CC 2.4.1.1: "A `key:revocation:v1` row is withdrawn by nobody, because revocation is non-rollbackable"
note: CC 3.4.1 closes the list of what revokes a root, a key or a conferral, and the list has no key:revocation row and no expiry; CC 2.4.1.1 and CC 3.2 (NotRooted past revoked_after) make the key:revocation row a carrier of its own. A reader resolves it; the closed list is short by two.

side_a: CC 2.4: "**Retraction of a cosigned row is by the same quorum**"
side_b: CC 2.4.1.1: "The withdrawal is cosigned under the same `consensus_protocol`, judged on the receiver's fold at the withdrawal's signed instant."
note: The same quorum can be read as the same signers; rule 0 means the same protocol over the roster as it stands at the withdrawal. The two differ after any roster change. Rule 0 is the home.

side_a: CC 3.2: "A node MUST reject a rule-2 or rule-4 `withdraws` against a live owner-binding unless it carries a `wa_adjudication_ref`."
side_b: manifests/transitions.json (ownership:{relation}:{target_kind}:{version}, withdraw): "when(verb=withdraw,has=wa_adjudication_ref) one wa_adjudication:{state}@admitted[id=ref:wa_adjudication_ref] else refuse"
note: The data puts the recovery guard on the ownership:* mirror row and fires it only when the reference is present; the owner-binding itself (self:delegates_to) has one transition, authorize, and no withdraw, supersede or lapse. The text's gate (a subject or delegate withdrawal with no reference is refused) and the owner's own withdrawal are not in the data.

side_a: CC 3.4.7.3: "A `federation_keys` key whose `identity_type` set contains `node` MUST NOT also contain `agent` or `user`."
side_b: CC 4.5.8.4: "Forbid any cohabitation at the wire layer (substrate enforces gates by membership; constitutional/substrate cohabitation discipline is consumer/operator policy per CC 4.5.8.1)"
note: CC 4.5.8.4 lists, under what the role-set rule does not do, forbidding any cohabitation, and leaves the discipline to operator policy. CC 3.4.7.1 and CC 3.4.7.3 Clause A forbid one pair with MUST NOT. A key record carrying node with agent is admitted on one reading and refused on the other. Clause A is the later and specific rule, and CC 3.2 leans on it.

side_a: CC 2.6.1.7: "the fingerprint the first ten lowercase base32 characters of sha256(ed25519 public key)"
side_b: CC 2.6.8: "SHOULD raise the fingerprint length (16 characters, 80 bits, moves the bound to 2⁴⁰)"
note: The format is stated as ten characters, normative, in CC 2.6.8 and in the signed-object table; the same paragraph of CC 2.6.8 tells a large deployment to use sixteen. A verifier that recomputes ten characters refuses a sixteen-character id. Nothing says how a reader learns which length a label uses.

side_a: CC 2.3.2.2: "the binding is itself a `delegates_to`-shaped attestation (`delegates_to(canonical_hash → newly_enrolled_key, scope: [identity_binding])`)"
side_b: CC 3.3.14: "A bare `scores` Contribution on the registered dimension **`identity:canonical_binding:{canonical_hash}`**"
note: Two wire shapes for one act, and two effects: CC 2.3.2.2 says the admitted binding lets the bound key withdraw under rule 2; CC 3.3.14 says it is a claim readers weigh that admits nothing. CC 3.3.14 is the later, normative entry and the registry row follows it.

side_a: CC 2.3.2.1: "A consumer verifies a `key_id`'s fingerprint suffix against the public key it obtains **at registration and at pairing**"
side_b: CC 2.6.8: "a consumer resolving a `key_id` MUST verify the fingerprint against the pubkey it obtains"
note: When the check runs: at registration and pairing only, or at every resolution. CC 2.6.8 holds the MUST and its own next sentence says a collision is caught at registration and never at resolution.

side_a: CC 3.1.3.2: "Expiry is judged on the instants the parties signed, never on a receiver's clock."
side_b: CC 4.5.13: "Every window of this table is measured by each node from the instant it first held the proposal, never from a signed instant of the proposer or of a cosigner."
note: Opposite clocks for a membership change. CC 3.1.3.2 concludes that every node gives the same verdict for the same rows; CC 4.5.13 (whose table has the invite and removal windows) concludes that two nodes may close a window at different moments, and adds that the first-held instant is what every window in this document runs from. That last sentence also contradicts CC 2.6.7 (W runs from the signed asserted_at) and CC 3.2 T4a (the attach window runs from a cosignature's signed_at). If the proposal's signed expiry and the policy window are two things, neither section says so.

side_a: CC 2.6.7: "The substrate MUST refuse such a row whose `asserted_at` precedes the receiver's clock by more than `W`"
side_b: CC 3.3.6.3: "A row signed by a key that is still live admits at any age"
note: Whether W binds every chain-judged row or only a row whose signer has lost standing at receipt. A new device syncing old consent rows or licences admits them on one reading and refuses them asserted_at_stale on the other. Open in the conflict table.

side_a: CC 2.6.7: "Consumers receiving an attestation whose `asserted_at` is more than 5 minutes in the future MUST reject it as malformed."
side_b: CC 3.1.3.1: "is applied once, at the emitter's own admitting substrate, and a row it admitted replicates as admitted"
note: Every receiving consumer applies the future bound, or only the first admitting substrate. CC 3.1.3.1 states its rule about the general clock rule in a parenthesis though it means session claims only.

side_a: CC 5.3.6.1: "`signed_at` exceeds [CC 2.6.7](part_2_the_grammar.md) ±5 minute tolerance"
side_b: CC 2.6.7: "Consumers receiving an attestation whose `asserted_at` is more than 5 minutes in the future MUST reject it as malformed."
note: The refusal names signed_at and a bound in both directions; the rule names asserted_at and bounds the future only. A row signed six minutes ago is refused under the table's wording and admitted under the rule.

side_a: CC 2.6.7: "the current consumer clock is within ±5 minutes of the substrate's network-consensus clock"
side_b: CC 4.4.3.2.4.1: "No global clock assumed."
note: The valid_until test needs a network-consensus clock that no section defines and that CC 4.4.3.2.4.1 says is not assumed.

side_a: CC 5.3.4: "a root attaches by the pinned `bundle_fingerprint`, with `attach_window_secs` **604800**"
side_b: CC 3.2: "With the quorum at `0` there is no timer and no obligation."
note: With witnessed mode off CC 5.3.4 still gives the charter a seven-day attach window; CC 3.2 says no cosignature counts and there is no timer, and the attach window is defined only over counted cosignatures. A reader of CC 5.3.4 alone has a window with nothing to measure, and may measure the bundle's age against it. CC 3.2 and CC 5.3.4's own "never its age" support the no-timer reading.

side_a: CC 3.4.5: "MUST be able to demonstrate over the [CC 3.1.5](part_3_the_namespace.md) `trace:complete:v1` record that no item violates the rule"
side_b: CC 5.3.2: "The trace that row anchors is carried as `trace:complete:v1` ([CC 3.1.5](part_3_the_namespace.md#3.1.5)) or its post-scrub `trace_summary:{kind}`."
note: The anti-Goodhart audit is owed over the complete trace; the substrate's duty is met by either the complete trace or its scrubbed summary, and an unacted deliberation keeps no trace at all (CC 1.13.6). Where only the summary is carried, the demonstration CC 3.4.5 requires has no record to run over. Neither section says which form the audit may use.

side_a: CC 3.1.7: "A substrate observing emission on a family with no registry row (provisional or ratified) MUST surface it as a conformance failure (`namespace_family_unregistered`), never admit-and-wait."
side_b: CC 3.1.7: "An unregistered family has no owning component, no polarity and no reserved rule, so a consumer resolving its authority falls through to the producer-steward default."
note: What a node does with a row on a family that has no registry row. R2 says it never admits under a defaulted authority; R1 says its authority resolves to the producer-steward default, and "Where the fallback remains" keeps that default for an open-vocabulary space it does not define (an unrowed family, or the open leaves of a registered one). R1 also calls an ungated family described only in CC 3.3 conformant though unregistered. The row is admitted on one reading and refused on the other. The closed-stem passages support refusal.

side_a: CC 4.5.13: "The standing is the roles the held rows give them: author, subject, member, moderator, founder, steward, holder, witness."
side_b: manifests/transitions.json (roles): ""registered""
note: The text gives eight standings. The transitions data uses 23 role names: it has no moderator and no witness (it uses the scope names moderate, review, takedown, slash, attest, serve), and it adds registered, self, owner, wa, operator, custodian, winner, tally and three identity:* roles. A queue built from the text's list cannot match most transitions' roles.
